To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated the light-induced resistive switching behavior of the Nb NNF devices in visible and NIR range and the corresponding photo-response can be understood by the photon assisted scattering of electron-phonon system.
we demonstrate the photo-switching and bolometeric behavior of Nb thin film superconductors in the nanostructured regime.
we report a room temperature opto-electronic switching behavior in Nb nanostructures which is explained by a light assisted electron-phononic scattering mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the optoelectronic properties of superconducting Nb thin films.
the study of optical and transport property of nanostructured Nb thin film.
the investigation of the photo-response of the NNFs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NNF devices exhibit photo-resistive switching at room temperature and superconducting phase slip based bolometric behavior at low temperature.
the nanostructured superconductors are not only the best superconductors but also the best photon detectors.
the Nb nanostructures are promising for future optoelectronic device applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Nb is not just a superconductor but it can be used as an optical switch at room temperature.
we demonstrate the photo-responsivity and bolometric features in Nb thin films and the corresponding mechanism is explained in terms of light induced electron-phonon interaction.
the NNFs are capable of sensing the light in a wide range of temperatures, which is a rare property for any other material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NNFs are promising for the development of room temperature optoelectronic devices.
the superconductor Nb is also capable of sensing light in the visible and near infrared region of electromagnetic spectrum.
the NNFs can act as a room temperature photon detector and a bolometer in its superconductivity phase.
